mainTopic: Why 'everyone' lists are needed: כהנים in שופר, מגילה, זימון, and ערכין, and the ברייתא on who can be valued
overview: The גמרא goes through a series of ברייתות that say 'everyone, כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים' is obligated in something. Each time it asks 'פשיטא, isn't that obvious?' and then finds the special case that makes the ruling necessary: שופר, מקרא מגילה (people stop their מקדש service to hear it), being obligated in זימון (even כהנים eating קדשים), and joining a זימון (a כהן eating תרומה with a זר eating חולין). Then it asks the same question about our own משנה, which says everyone can make an ערכין vow. רבא first ties the answer to בן בוכרי, who held that כהנים don't give the half-shekel, and the גמרא explains that view. אביי rejects that reason and suggests a link to פדיון הבן instead. רבא knocks that down from the איל אשם and gives a final reason: 'set before the כהן' might have seemed to leave out a כהן. Finally the גמרא asks for the source that a מנוול and a מוכה שחין can be valued. It begins a ברייתא that reads the words בערכך and נפשות to teach who can and cannot be valued, and that ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the שופר ruling is needed for כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining why we might have thought כהנים are exempt from שופר on ראש השנה, and why they are obligated after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since כהנים and לוים can redeem their fields at any time, you might think they are also exempt from the מצוה of ראש השנה. So the ברייתא teaches us that they are obligated. True, they are not part of the release of land, but they are still part of the release of money and the freeing of slaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer to 'isn't it obvious?' about כהנים and שופר. It shows the mistaken idea and then corrects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the land laws of יובל don't apply to כהנים and לוים, one might think the related מצוה of ראש השנה doesn't apply to them either. The answer is that יובל is not only about land. כהנים are still part of the release of money and the freeing of slaves, so they are included.

keyTerms.meaning: they may redeem (their sold land) at any time
it teaches us (something we might not have known)
the release of land (land going back to its owner)
the release of money (loans being cancelled)
sending slaves free

steps.whatToRemember: כהנים are exempt from only one part of the יובל-type laws (land). They are still part of the other parts, so they are obligated in שופר.

phrases.english: and they redeem at any time,
phrases.notes: "They" are the כהנים and לוים, from the line just before.

phrases.english: I might say that in the מצוה of Rosh HaShana
phrases.notes: The מצוה here is blowing the שופר, which the ברייתא was talking about.

phrases.english: they should also not be obligated,
so it teaches us:
granted that they are not included in the release of land,
in the release of money and in the sending free of slaves
at least they are included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'לא צריכא' answer that began on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a partial inclusion: excluded from one part of the law, included in the others
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since land release doesn't apply to כהנים, they should be exempt from the מצוה of ראש השנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are still included in the release of money and of slaves, so they are obligated.

steps.title: Everyone is obligated in reading the מגילה
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא says כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים are all obligated in מקרא מגילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone is obligated in reading the מגילה: כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא with the same 'everyone' wording, now about the מגילה. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the שופר ruling, this one lists all three groups. That invites the same question: why say something that seems obvious?

keyTerms.meaning: everyone is obligated
the reading of מגילת אסתר on פורים

phrases.english: Everyone is obligated in the reading of the Megillah,
priests, Levites, and Israelites.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא following the same pattern as the שופר one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים are all obligated in מקרא מגילה.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs to list כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: why would anyone think any of these groups is exempt from מגילה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: מגילה is a מצוה for every Jew, and nothing seems to exempt כהנים or לוים. So the extra wording seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: it is obvious (so why say it?)

phrases.english: That's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the wording of the ברייתא in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The listing of כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים in the מגילה ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nobody would think these groups are exempt, so the list seems pointless.

steps.title: They must stop their Temple service
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed to teach that those serving in the מקדש stop their עבודה to hear the מגילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed to teach that they stop their service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is teaching something new: even in the middle of מקדש service, you stop to hear the מגילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is not that these groups are obligated. That part is obvious. The new point is that מגילה comes before their important service in the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: it is only needed for (a special case)
to stop their service

phrases.english: No, it is needed
to teach that they cancel their service,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'פשיטא' challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a new point hidden in the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Their מקדש service might come first, so they would skip the מגילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: They stop their service to hear the מגילה.

steps.title: Support from רב יהודה in the name of שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its answer with רב יהודה's teaching in the name of שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: כהנים at their service, לוים on their platform, and ישראלים at their מעמד all stop their service and come to hear the מגילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that its answer matches a known teaching of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל names all three groups, each at its own job in the מקדש. All three stop to hear the מגילה. That is exactly why the ברייתא lists all three.

keyTerms.meaning: the service of the כהנים in the מקדש
the platform where the לוים sang
the group of ישראלים who stood by during the קרבנות הציבור

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that קריאת המגילה takes priority even over מקדש service.

phrases.english: and this is like what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel,
as Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
priests at their service,
and Levites on their platform,
and Israelites at their watch,
cancel their service
and come to hear the reading of the Megillah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 4 with an אמורא's teaching.
steps.raayaObject: That those serving in the מקדש stop their service for the מגילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל

steps.title: Everyone is obligated in זימון
steps.stepSummary: A third ברייתא says כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים are all obligated in זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone is obligated in זימון: כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more 'everyone' ברייתא, now about זימון before ברכת המזון. This sets up the same question again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once again all three groups are listed. That makes us expect the same 'isn't it obvious?' challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: the group invitation to bentch when three or more eat together

phrases.english: Everyone is obligated in zimmun,
priests, Levites, and Israelites.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא in the same pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים are all obligated in זימון.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again asks why the list is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges this ברייתא as well. Why would anyone think these groups don't make a זימון?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anyone who eats a meal bentches, so listing the groups seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: the three groups of the Jewish people

phrases.english: That's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the wording in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The listing of the three groups in the זימון ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Everyone who eats bentches, so the list seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The case of כהנים eating קדשים
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed for כהנים eating קדשים, which might seem like an act of atonement rather than a regular meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for when they eat קדשים. You might have thought: the Torah says 'they shall eat those things with which atonement was made,' and this eating is an act of כפרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the special case: כהנים eating קדשים. It also explains why we might have thought they don't make a זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק shows that the כהנים' eating brings כפרה to the owners. So you might think this is a מצוה act and not a normal meal, which would mean no זימון. This is only the mistaken idea, and the next step corrects it.

keyTerms.meaning: sacrificial meat
it would have entered your mind to say (the mistaken assumption)
atonement
the Merciful One (the Torah)

steps.confusionAlert: The part starting with סלקא דעתך אמינא is NOT the final הלכה. It is only the idea we might have had, which the גמרא is about to reject.

phrases.english: No, it is needed where they are eating sacrificial meat.
It would have entered your mind to say:
"And they shall eat those things with which atonement was made"
phrases.notes: שמות 29:33

phrases.english: the Merciful One said,
and this is atonement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'פשיטא' challenge of step 7 by naming the special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a new point hidden in the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Eating קדשים is an act of כפרה, not a meal, so there would be no זימון.
steps.terutzMaskana: Given in the next step: there is still a זימון.

steps.title: Eating and being satisfied requires bentching
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that since the Torah ties bentching to eating and being full, כהנים eating קדשים still make a זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it teaches us: the Torah said 'and you shall eat and be satisfied,' and here there is eating and being satisfied.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the mistaken idea and gives the final ruling. כהנים eating קדשים must make a זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What creates the obligation of ברכת המזון is the eating and being full, not the purpose of the meal. Even if the eating also brings כפרה, the כהנים still ate and are satisfied, so they bentch with a זימון.

keyTerms.meaning: and you shall eat and be satisfied (the source of ברכת המזון)
Grace after Meals
they are present / it is there

steps.whatToRemember: The obligation to bentch depends on eating and being full. Even an eating that is a מצוה, or that brings כפרה, still needs ברכת המזון and a זימון.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a basic rule: the purpose of a meal does not cancel the obligation to bentch on it.

phrases.english: So it teaches us,
"And you shall eat and be satisfied," the Merciful One said,
phrases.notes: דברים 8:10

phrases.english: and here those are present.
phrases.notes: He means that the כהנים really did eat and become full, so the פסוק applies to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: קא משמע לן ואכלת ושבעת אמר רחמנא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the mistaken idea of step 8 and gives the final ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: כהנים eating קדשים are obligated in זימון, because they ate and were satisfied.

steps.title: Everyone joins together for a זימון
steps.stepSummary: A fourth ברייתא teaches that כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים all join together to make a זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone joins together to make a זימון: כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another ברייתא that uses the same 'everyone' list. It is setting up the same question it asked about the earlier lists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said everyone is obligated in זימון. This ברייתא adds something new: people from the different groups can join each other to reach the number needed for a זימון.

keyTerms.meaning: join together (to complete the group needed for a זימון)
priests
Levites

phrases.english: Everyone joins together for a zimmun,
priests, Levites, and Israelites.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth 'everyone' ברייתא to the series, this time about joining together.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים can all join together to form a זימון.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs to say that all three groups join together.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: of course all Jews can join together for a זימון, so why say it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every Jew is obligated in בענטשן, so it seems clear that any of them can join together. The challenge forces the גמרא to find a case where the rule is actually needed.

phrases.english: That's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the list in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The list of כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים in the זימון ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If all Jews must bentch, it goes without saying that they can join together, so the list seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The case: כהנים eat תרומה while a זר eats regular food
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is needed for a case where the כהנים eat תרומה or קדשים, and the זר eats ordinary חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where the כהנים are eating תרומה or קדשים, and the זר is eating ordinary חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to a special case where the people at the table are eating different kinds of food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the כהנים are eating food that a זר is not allowed to touch. That makes it less obvious that they count as one group for a זימון.

keyTerms.meaning: the portion of produce given to כהנים; a non-כהן may not eat it
sacrificial meat
a non-כהן
ordinary, non-holy food

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where the priests are eating teruma or sacrificial meat,
and a non-priest is eating ordinary food.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּקָאָכְלִי כֹּהֲנִים תְּרוּמָה אוֹ קׇדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 11 by narrowing the ברייתא to a specific case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ruling to a specific case (אוקימתא).
steps.terutzMaskana: The list matters when the כהנים eat holy food that the זר may not eat.

steps.title: A כהן can eat the זר's food, so they join
steps.stepSummary: One might think they can't join because the זר can't share the כהן's food, but the כהן can share the זר's food, so they do join.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since the זר couldn't eat with the כהן even if he wanted to, he shouldn't join. So the ברייתא teaches us: even though a זר can't eat with a כהן, a כהן can eat with a זר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what we would have wrongly thought, and what the ברייתא teaches instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistaken idea was that people who can't share one meal can't join for a זימון. The answer is that sharing only has to work one way: the כהן is allowed to eat the זר's חולין, so they can count as eating together.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have thought (the mistaken first idea)
so it teaches us
granted that, even though
together with

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן and a זר can join for a זימון even when the כהן eats תרומה, because the כהן could still eat the זר's ordinary food.

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְאִי בָּעֵי זָר לְמֵיכַל בַּהֲדֵי כֹּהֵן
phrases.english: since if a non-priest wanted to eat together with a priest
he could not eat,
phrases.notes: "He" is the זר, who can't eat the כהן's תרומה.

phrases.english: I would say he should not join.
So it teaches us:

phrases.aramaic: נְהִי דְּזָר בַּהֲדֵי כֹּהֵן לָא מָצֵי אָכֵיל,
phrases.english: granted that a non-priest cannot eat with a priest,
a priest can eat with a non-priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וְאִי בָּעֵי זָר לְמֵיכַל בַּהֲדֵי כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reasoning behind the case given in Step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the זר can't eat the כהן's food, they don't count as one group.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהן can eat the זר's food, so they can join.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Being able to share food in one direction is enough to join for a זימון.

steps.title: Back to our משנה: everyone can make a valuation vow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to our משנה, which says כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים can all make an ערכין vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone can make a valuation vow: כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the opening line of our own משנה. It is setting up the same 'isn't that obvious?' question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the earlier ברייתות were examples of 'everyone' lists. Now the גמרא uses the same question on our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: make an ערכין vow, pledging a person's fixed Torah value to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Everyone can make a valuation vow,
priests, Levites, and Israelites.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side ברייתות and returns to the main משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים can all make ערכין vows.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious for our משנה too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why our משנה needs to list the three groups.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה: why would anyone think a כהן or לוי couldn't make an ערכין vow?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing obvious would exclude כהנים or לוים from ערכין. So spelling them out looks unnecessary.

phrases.english: That's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the list in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The list of כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים in our משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There seems to be no reason to think any group would be left out of ערכין.

steps.title: רבא: It is needed because of בן בוכרי
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the list is needed only because of the view of בן בוכרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is needed only because of בן בוכרי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers that the משנה lists כהנים because of a particular opinion. The גמרא now quotes that opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן בוכרי held a view about כהנים and the half-shekel. רבא suggests that view could make us think כהנים are left out of ערכין too. Step 22 explains the exact link, after the גמרא quotes and discusses בן בוכרי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: it is needed only for

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is needed only according to ben Bukhri,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְבֶן בּוּכְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 15 by pointing to a specific opinion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ties the משנה's wording to a specific opinion that needed to be countered.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list is needed because of בן בוכרי's view about כהנים.

steps.title: בן בוכרי: a כהן who gives the half-shekel is not a sinner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: בן בוכרי testified in יבנה that a כהן who gives the half-shekel does nothing wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי יהודה said, בן בוכרי testified in יבנה: Any כהן who gives the shekel is not a sinner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for בן בוכרי's opinion that רבא mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying a כהן who gives 'is not a sinner' implies he does not have to give. So in בן בוכרי's view, כהנים are not obligated in the half-shekel.

keyTerms.meaning: testified (reported a teaching before the חכמים)
gives the half-shekel
a sinner

steps.confusionAlert: בן בוכרי is not saying that giving is a מצוה for a כהן. He means a כהן is not required to give, but it isn't wrong if he does.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:
Rabbi Yehuda said:
Ben Bukhri testified in Yavne:
Any priest who gives the shekel is not a sinner.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הֵעִיד בֶּן בּוּכְרִי בְּיַבְנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the opinion רבא cited.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that there is a view treating כהנים differently.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in שקלים quoting בן בוכרי's testimony in יבנה.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי: a כהן who doesn't give is a sinner
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי disagrees: a כהן who doesn't give the half-shekel is a sinner, but כהנים twist a פסוק about a כהן's מנחה to excuse themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said to him: Not so. Rather, any כהן who does not give the shekel is a sinner. But the כהנים interpret this פסוק in their own favor: 'And every meal offering of a כהן shall be completely burned; it shall not be eaten.'
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the same משנה, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי rejects בן בוכרי's view and says כהנים are obligated like everyone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view כהנים must give the half-shekel, and a כהן who doesn't is a sinner. He explains that some כהנים use the פסוק about a כהן's מנחה to argue their way out of giving.

keyTerms.meaning: interpret, expound (a פסוק)
for themselves, in their own favor
a meal offering brought by a כהן
completely burned

steps.whatToRemember: בן בוכרי held that כהנים don't have to give the half-shekel. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי held that they do, and that those who don't are misusing a פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי:
phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said to him:
Not so,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כׇּל כֹּהֵן שֶׁאֵינוֹ שׁוֹקֵל חוֹטֵא,
phrases.english: rather, any priest who does not give the shekel is a sinner,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁהַכֹּהֲנִים דּוֹרְשִׁין מִקְרָא זֶה לְעַצְמָן:
phrases.english: but the priests interpret this verse in their own favor:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְכׇל מִנְחַת כֹּהֵן כָּלִיל תִּהְיֶה לֹא תֵאָכֵל״.
phrases.english: "And every meal offering of a priest shall be completely burned; it shall not be eaten."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:16

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי: לֹא כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quoted משנה with the disagreement with בן בוכרי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects בן בוכרי's claim that כהנים are not obligated in the half-shekel.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: כהנים are obligated like all Jews; the פסוק they rely on is being used in their own favor.

steps.title: The כהנים finish their argument for not giving
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה completes the כהנים' reasoning: if the communal מנחות were partly theirs, they would have to be fully burned and could not be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the עומר, the שתי הלחם, and the לחם הפנים would then be ours, how could they be eaten?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the כהנים' excuse from the משנה brought in the last step. It spells out exactly how they twist the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Communal מנחות are bought with half-shekel money. If כהנים gave money, these מנחות would partly belong to כהנים, and a כהן's מנחה must be fully burned. Since these מנחות are eaten, the כהנים claim they must not be allowed to give.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן
The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות
The showbread placed on the שולחן each שבת

phrases.english: Since the omer and the two loaves
and the showbread would be ours,
how could they be eaten?
phrases.notes: A כהן's מנחה must be completely burned (ויקרא 6:16), yet these are eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וְעוֹמֶר וּשְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם וְלֶחֶם הַפָּנִים שֶׁלָּנוּ הֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quotation of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's description of how the כהנים excuse themselves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים argue that giving half-shekels would make the communal מנחות count as כהנים' מנחות, which may not be eaten.

steps.title: Even according to בן בוכרי, a giving כהן should be a sinner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why בן בוכרי says a כהן who gives does nothing wrong. Since he is not obligated, his money would bring non-holy funds into the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to בן בוכרי too: since כהנים are not obligated to bring it in the first place, even when one brings it he is a sinner, because he brings חולין into the עזרה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges בן בוכרי's statement that a כהן who gives the half-shekel has not sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The half-shekel funds communal offerings. If a כהן is not obligated, his coins are not really part of the community's required money. So offerings bought with them seem to be improper, like bringing חולין into the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start / in the first place
A sinner
Non-holy, ordinary items
The בית המקדש courtyard

phrases.english: And according to ben Bukhri too,
since from the start they are not obligated to bring it,
even when he does bring it, he is a sinner,
for he is bringing non-holy items into the courtyard!
phrases.notes: The idea is that offerings bought with money he didn't owe wouldn't count as proper communal offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's view back to בן בוכרי's view and questions it.
steps.kashyaTarget: בן בוכרי's statement that a כהן who gives the half-shekel is not a sinner
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he is not obligated, his coins are not communal money, so using them for communal offerings brings חולין into the עזרה.

steps.title: He hands the money over to the community
steps.stepSummary: The כהן gives his half-shekel and fully transfers it to the community, so it becomes communal money.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brings them and hands them over to the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the כהן gives his coins over to the community completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the coins are handed over to the community, they are no longer his private money. Offerings bought with them are fully communal, so there is no problem of חולין in the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Handed over / transferred
The community

phrases.english: He brings them
and hands them over to the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the gift becomes communal property
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כהן's voluntary half-shekel stays his own private money, so it would be חולין.
steps.terutzMaskana: He transfers it fully to the צבור, so it counts as communal money.

steps.title: Why בן בוכרי's view makes the משנה's list necessary
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק links ערכין to the שקל הקדש. So we might think that כהנים, who are exempt from שקלים according to בן בוכרי, are also outside ערכין. The משנה teaches that they are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since it is written 'וכל ערכך יהיה בשקל הקדש', whoever is included in שקלים is included in ערכין. Then these כהנים, who are not included in שקלים, would not be included in ערכין. So the משנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains רבא's answer from step 16: why בן בוכרי's view creates a need to list כהנים in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק joins ערכין and שקל, which suggests that the two go together. According to בן בוכרי כהנים are exempt from שקלים, so we might have excluded them from ערכין. By listing כהנים, the משנה shows they are still included in ערכין.

keyTerms.meaning: It would have entered your mind (a mistaken first thought)
The holy shekel, the standard coin of the מקדש
The yearly half-shekel obligation
Vows to give a person's fixed Torah value
It teaches us (the point the source is making)

steps.whyThisMatters: This finally explains רבא's claim that the list in our משנה exists only because of בן בוכרי.

phrases.english: It would have entered your mind to say:
since it is written
"And all your valuations shall be according to the shekel of the Sanctuary,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:25

phrases.english: whoever is included in the shekels
is included in valuations,
and these priests,
since they are not included in the shekels,
are not included in valuations,
so it teaches us otherwise.
phrases.notes: "It" is our משנה, which lists כהנים to show they are included in ערכין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side question about בן בוכרי to explain רבא's answer to step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a possible mistaken assumption that the משנה comes to block
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because ערכין is linked to the שקל, כהנים, who are exempt from שקלים according to בן בוכרי, would be exempt from ערכין too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists כהנים to teach that they are included in ערכין anyway.

steps.title: אביי: that פסוק teaches a minimum of a סלע
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא: the פסוק 'וכל ערכך' is needed to teach that no ערך is less than a סלע, so it cannot link ערכין to the שקלים obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: this 'וכל ערכך' comes to teach that all ערכין you assess should not be less than a סלע!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's explanation by showing that the פסוק has a different job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's mistaken first thought relied on the פסוק linking ערכין to שקלים. אביי says the פסוק teaches the minimum amount of a ערך, which is one סלע. If so, there was no reason to think כהנים are outside ערכין, and the question of why the משנה lists them returns.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin equal to one שקל
Assess or set a ערך

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבא, who gave the answer in step 16.

phrases.english: This "and all your valuations"
is to teach that all valuations that you assess
should not be less than a sela
phrases.notes: Even a poor person who pays based on what he can afford must give at least one סלע.

phrases.english: that is what it comes for!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of רבא's answer given in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'וכל ערכך יהיה בשקל הקדש' links ערכין to the half-shekel obligation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is already used to teach that every ערך must be at least a סלע, so it cannot support the mistaken thought that רבא's explanation depends on.

steps.title: אביי's reason: one might link ערכין to redeeming a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the משנה must include כהנים because we might have thought that only people who are part of פדיון הבן are part of ערכין, and כהנים are not part of פדיון הבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: The משנה had to say it. You might have thought this: since the פסוק about the firstborn says 'redeem them according to your valuation', anyone who is part of פדיון הבן is part of ערכין. Then these כהנים, who are not part of פדיון הבן, would not be part of ערכין. So the משנה teaches us that they are included.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי, who just rejected רבא's reason, now gives his own reason why the משנה had to say that כהנים are included in ערכין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The firstborn פסוק uses the word 'בערכך' (your valuation), the same word used for ערכין. So one might link the two: whoever is not in פדיון הבן is also not in ערכין. כהנים are exempt from פדיון הבן, so without the משנה we might have exempted them from ערכין too.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary (to state this)
You might have thought to say (the mistaken idea)
Redeeming a firstborn son with five shekels
According to your valuation, the word that links פסוקים to ערכין
It teaches us (that the mistaken idea is wrong)

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said: It was necessary,
it might enter your mind to say:
Since it is written
“And their redemption, from a month old you shall redeem, according to your valuation,”
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:16

phrases.english: anyone who is included in redemption of the firstborn son
is included in valuations,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָנֵי כֹּהֲנִים הוֹאִיל וְלֵיתַנְהוּ בְּפִדְיוֹן הַבֵּן —
phrases.english: and these priests, since they are not included in redemption of the firstborn son,
are not included in valuations.
So it teaches us (that they are included).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבא's link to שקלים in step 23, אביי gives a different reason the משנה needed to include כהנים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New הוה אמינא based on a different פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the firstborn פסוק says 'בערכך', only people included in פדיון הבן would be included in ערכין, so כהנים would be left out.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches that כהנים are included in ערכין.

steps.title: רבא objects using the ram of the guilt offering
steps.stepSummary: רבא says אביי's logic proves too much. The איל אשם פסוק also says 'בערכך', so a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס, who are not in ערכין, would not bring an איל אשם, and that cannot be right.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If so, look at the איל אשם. It is written 'And he shall bring his guilt offering to ה׳, a ram without blemish from the flock, according to your valuation.' Would you also say that anyone in ערכין is in איל אשם? Then a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס, who are not in ערכין, would not be in איל אשם!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's answer. He shows that the same word 'בערכך' appears in another place, and linking the two topics there leads to a result nobody accepts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the shared word 'בערכך' means 'same people in both topics', then it should work for the איל אשם too. But a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are left out of ערכין and still clearly bring an איל אשם. So the word 'בערכך' does not create a 'same people' link, and אביי's הוה אמינא falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: If that is so (introducing a result that seems absurd)
The ram brought as a guilt offering
A person whose sex cannot be determined
A person with both male and female features

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying a טומטום is exempt from the איל אשם. He is saying the opposite: everyone agrees they must bring it, so אביי's way of reading 'בערכך' must be wrong.

phrases.english: Rava said to him: If that is so,
regarding the ram of the guilt offering, as it is written:
“And he shall bring his guilt offering to the Lord,
a ram without blemish from the flock, according to your valuation,”
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:25

phrases.english: so too, would anyone who is included in valuations
be included in the ram of the guilt offering,
and a tumtum and a hermaphrodite, who are not included in valuations,
would not be included in the ram of the guilt offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks אביי's answer in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's idea that the shared word 'בערכך' links who is included in two different topics.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Applying the same reading to the איל אשם would exempt a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס from it, which is clearly wrong, so the reading itself is wrong.

steps.title: A new reason: a כהן might not be set before another כהן
steps.stepSummary: רבא (some say רב אשי) explains that the משנה must include כהנים because the פסוק says the poor person is set before the כהן, and one might think a כהן cannot be set before another כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said, and some say it was רב אשי: The משנה had to say it. You might have thought: since it is written 'he shall be set before the כהן', but not a כהן before a כהן, a כהן is not included. So the משנה teaches us that he is included.
steps.whatsHappening: Since אביי's reason was rejected, רבא (or רב אשי) gives a third reason why the משנה had to include כהנים in ערכין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about a poor person who cannot pay the full ערך says he is set before the כהן to be assessed. One might have thought this assumes the person being assessed is not a כהן, so a כהן would be left out of ערכין. The משנה teaches that a כהן is included, and another כהן can assess him.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall be set before the כהן (to be assessed)

steps.whatToRemember: Three reasons were given for why the משנה needs to include כהנים: a link to שקלים (rejected), a link to פדיון הבן (rejected), and the final one: 'set before the כהן' might have seemed to leave out a כהן.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אָשֵׁי: אִיצְטְרִיךְ,
phrases.english: Rather, Rava said, and some say it was Rav Ashi: It was necessary,
it might enter your mind to say,
since it is written: “Then he shall be set before the priest,”
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:8, about a poor person who cannot pay the full ערך.

phrases.english: but not a priest before a priest,
so it teaches us (that priests are included).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אָשֵׁי: אִיצְטְרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's answer, which was knocked down in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New הוה אמינא from a different פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the פסוק says the person is set before the כהן, one might think a כהן cannot be valued before another כהן, so כהנים are not in ערכין.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a מנוול and a מוכה שחין can be valued?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the word 'נערכין' in the משנה, which was said earlier (2a) to include a מנוול and a מוכה שחין, and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Are valued': this comes to include a repulsive person and one with boils. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It brings back an earlier explanation of the משנה and asks for its source, setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said that the word 'נערכין' includes a מנוול and a מוכה שחין. They have no value on the market, but they still get the fixed ערך set by the תורה. Now the גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: To include (this comes to add)
A repulsive-looking person
A person suffering from boils
From where do we know these things? (asking for the source)

phrases.english: “Are valued”: to include a repulsive person and one afflicted with boils.
phrases.notes: This goes back to a word in the משנה that the גמרא explained this way earlier, on 2a.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of כהנים and opens a new question about another part of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches that a מנוול and a מוכה שחין are valued under the תורה's fixed ערכין.

steps.title: The answer begins with a ברייתא on 'בערכך'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers Step 27 by quoting a ברייתא. Its first teaching is that the word 'בערכך' includes a ערך סתום.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Sages taught: 'According to your valuation' comes to include an unspecified valuation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering the question about the source for including a מנוול and a מוכה שחין by quoting a ברייתא. Its first line explains the word 'בערכך'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא goes through the words of the ערכין פסוקים one by one. Its first teaching is that 'בערכך' includes a ערך סתום, a valuation that was not spelled out. The part that answers our question comes further on, so keep reading.

keyTerms.meaning: 'According to your valuation': a word in the ערכין פסוק (ויקרא 27:2)
An unspecified valuation, one that was not spelled out
'To include': this word in the פסוק adds a case

steps.confusionAlert: Don't expect the very first line of the ברייתא to answer the question about the מנוול. The גמרא quotes the whole ברייתא, and the relevant piece comes later.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
phrases.notes: This is the answer to Step 27's question: where do we learn that a מנוול and a מוכה שחין are valued?

phrases.english: 'According to your valuation' — to include an unspecified valuation.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 27 by bringing a ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא that explains the ערכין פסוקים word by word, starting with 'בערכך' including a ערך סתום

steps.title: You value a whole person, not a limb
steps.stepSummary: A second reading of 'בערכך': a person gives the ערך of a whole person, not the ערך of a limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'according to your valuation' means he gives the valuation of his whole self, not the valuation of limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second, different reading of 'בערכך'. It says ערכין applies to a whole person and not to a body part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בערכך' is read as 'your value,' meaning your whole self. So if someone pledges the ערך of a hand or a foot, he owes nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Another explanation': a different reading of the same word
The valuation of the whole person
The valuation of limbs or body parts

phrases.english: Alternatively: 'According to your valuation' —
he gives the valuation of his entire self,
and not the valuation of limbs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative reading of the same word 'בערכך'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ערכין applies to a whole person. A pledge of the ערך of a limb has no effect.

steps.title: A limb you cannot live without counts as the whole person
steps.stepSummary: Someone might think that even a vital limb is left out. The word 'נפשות' teaches that a limb the life depends on does count.
steps.simpleTranslation: I might have thought I should exclude even a part that the soul depends on. So the פסוק says 'persons'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible mistake: maybe even a vital organ is left out like other limbs. It answers from the word 'נפשות'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 left out the ערך of limbs. A limb a person cannot live without is different, because pledging it is like pledging the person's life. 'נפשות' (souls, lives) teaches that such a pledge counts as the ערך of the whole person.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think': introduces a wrong idea that the ברייתא will reject
A body part the life depends on (like the liver)
'The פסוק teaches': brings the proof from the פסוק
'Persons' or 'souls' (ויקרא 27:2)

phrases.english: One might think that I exclude
even an item upon which the soul depends?
phrases.notes: He means a body part you can't live without, so pledging it is really pledging the whole person.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'persons,'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of Step 29: a vital limb is an exception
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pledging the ערך of a vital limb obligates the ערך of the whole person

steps.title: A dead person cannot be valued
steps.stepSummary: The word 'נפשות' also teaches that only a living person can be valued, not a dead one.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Persons': living persons, and not the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reads 'נפשות' a second way: it means living souls, so a dead person is left out of ערכין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'נפשות' means beings with a soul, which is to say alive. A person who values a dead body has said nothing, and he owes nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: A dead person

phrases.english: 'Persons' — and not the dead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further derivation from the same word 'נפשות'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dead person is not subject to ערכין

steps.title: A dying person (גוסס) cannot be valued either
steps.stepSummary: Someone might think only the dead are left out, not a גוסס. 'והעמיד והעריך' teaches that whoever cannot be stood before the כהן cannot be valued.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should I exclude the dead but not exclude a dying person? The פסוק says 'he shall be set… and he shall value': anyone who can be set up can be valued, and anyone who cannot be set up cannot be valued.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks whether a גוסס, who is still alive, might be included. It answers from the פסוק about setting the person before the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוסס is still a living 'נפש', so 'נפשות' alone would not leave him out. But the פסוק links valuing to 'setting before the כהן'. A גוסס cannot be stood up or moved, so he cannot be valued.

keyTerms.meaning: A person on his deathbed who is still alive
Being stood or set before the כהן
Being valued for ערכין

steps.whatToRemember: Two conditions to be valued: you must be alive ('נפשות'), and you must be able to be 'set before the כהן' ('והעמיד והעריך'). A גוסס fails the second one.

phrases.english: Should I exclude the dead,
but not exclude the dying person?
The verse says: 'He shall be set… and he shall value' —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:8. This is the same פסוק Step 26 used about setting the poor person before the כהן.

phrases.english: anyone who can be set up can be valued,
and anyone who cannot be set up cannot be valued.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹצִיא אֶת הַמֵּת, וְלֹא אוֹצִיא אֶת הַגּוֹסֵס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the exclusion of Step 31 from the dead to the גוסס
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוסס is not subject to ערכין, because he cannot be set before the כהן

steps.title: One person can value a hundred people
steps.stepSummary: A different reading of 'נפשות' in the plural: one person can pledge the ערך of many people, even a hundred.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'persons.' I would only know about one person who valued one person. Where do we learn that one person can value a hundred? The פסוק says 'persons'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reads the plural form of 'נפשות' a new way: it teaches that a single pledge can cover many people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Had the פסוק said 'נפש' (one person), we might have limited it to one pledger and one person being valued. The plural tells us that one person can pledge the ערך of a hundred people, and he owes each one's ערך.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I only know': the narrow reading before the פסוק widens it
'From where do we know?'
He pledged someone's ערך

phrases.english: Alternatively: 'Persons,'

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא אֶחָד שֶׁהֶעֱרִיךְ אֶחָד,
phrases.english: I only know of one who valued one,
from where do we know one who valued a hundred?
The verse says: 'Persons.'
phrases.notes: The point is the plural: 'souls,' not 'a soul.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״נְפָשֹׁת״, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא אֶחָד שֶׁהֶעֱרִיךְ אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative reading of 'נפשות', based on its plural form
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One person can pledge the ערך of many people at once

steps.title: Starting one more reading of 'נפשות'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins yet another explanation of 'נפשות'. The explanation itself continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'persons,'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The ברייתא opens one more reading of 'נפשות', and the content comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is taught yet. The ברייתא is getting ready for another reading of the plural 'נפשות', which may lead toward the answer about the מנוול and the מוכה שחין asked about in Step 27.

phrases.english: Alternatively: 'Persons,'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens another alternative reading of the same word, continued on the next amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only. The reading continues on the next amud.
